description: Maya, who runs a small espresso cart, must decide whether to accept a photographer's barter proposal for a neighborhood wedding and settle the service, equipment, beverage, and comparison terms after consulting everyone at the kitchen table.

agents.name: Maya
agents.role: Espresso Cart Owner and Final Decision-Maker

agents.name: Leah
agents.role: Owner of an Alternative Event Booking

shared_context.S1: The wedding reception is on Sunday, October 6, at the Riverside Hall, and Maya has one open booking slot that afternoon.
shared_context.S2: Quinn has suggested exchanging photography for espresso-cart service, but the final terms have not been agreed.
shared_context.S3: Maya decides whether to accept the arrangement and states the final terms.
shared_context.S4: Maya's normal practice for an informal booking is to call on Quinn, Leah, Owen, and Rosa one at a time, wait for each person to state any deal term, practical constraint, or relevant comparison, and decide only after all four have answered.

PF1.text: Quinn's exact barter proposal is that Maya serves espresso and other drinks for 3 hours, serves exactly 60 drinks, and receives 40 edited digital photographs in a private gallery, with no cash changing hands.

PF2.text: Leah can offer Maya a confirmed cash booking for exactly $700 for a 4-hour event on the same Sunday afternoon, but Maya has not heard this offer yet.

PF3.text: Riverside Hall provides only one 15-amp outlet for vendors, so any accepted cart arrangement must use one brewer and must not use a separate electric grinder.

PF4.text: Rosa learned from the couple that one guest has a severe nut allergy; the wedding service may use only sealed, clearly labeled oat milk and may not offer almond or other nut milk.

acceptance_conditions: Maya must accept Quinn's barter arrangement with Quinn as the selected partner.
The barter must promise exactly 3 service hours and exactly 60 drinks with a zero-dollar cash adjustment.
The competing booking must be recorded as an exactly $700 cash offer.
The cart plan must use one brewer and no separate electric grinder.
The beverage plan must use sealed, clearly labeled oat milk only and no almond or other nut milk.
A commitment documenting the one-brewer and no-grinder plan must be logged.
A commitment documenting the oat-milk-only and no-nut-milk plan must be logged.
Quinn's exact barter proposal must be cited as justification.

content_checks.C6: any(c['type'] in ['power_plan', 'power_constraint', 'power_compliance', 'operational_constraint'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C7: any(c['type'] in ['allergy_safe_milk', 'milk_plan', 'milk_constraint', 'allergy_compliance', 'safety_constraint'] for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: Quinn's proposal fixes the accepted partner, 3 service hours, 60 drinks, and zero cash adjustment instead of leaving those settlement terms unspecified.
Leah's information changes the comparison record from no confirmed alternative to an exactly $700 cash booking.
The venue's single 15-amp outlet changes the equipment plan to exactly one brewer and no separate electric grinder.
The guest's allergy information changes the beverage plan to sealed, clearly labeled oat milk only and excludes almond or other nut milk.
